Enapter
Enapter is the organization associated with the patented AEM electrolyser, providing the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 and its technical information.<SEP>Enapter is the manufacturer associated with the EL 4.0 electrolyser, its patented anion exchange membrane technology, and Enapter EMS.

AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0
AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 is Enapter's patented anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyser, a standardised, stackable and flexible system to produce on-site hydrogen. The modular design and advanced software integration allow set up in minutes and remote control and management.

Anion Exchange Membrane (AEM)
Anion exchange membrane (AEM) is Enapter's patented membrane technology used in the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.

Hydrogen
Hydrogen is the product generated on-site by the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.<SEP>Hydrogen is the product generated by the EL 4.0 water electrolysis process, with production rate up to 500 NL/h, up to 1.0785 kg/24 h, and purity depending on output pressure.<SEP>Hydrogen (H2, CAS 1333-74-0, EC 215-605-7) is a compressed gas with purity ≥99.8%. It is extremely flammable, contains gas under pressure, and may explode if heated.<SEP>Hydrogen is the chemical substance identified by chemical name Hydrogen, chemical formula H2, CAS no. 1333-74-0, and EC no. 215-605-7. Hydrogen is a single substance rather than a mixture and is described as a high-purity compressed gas. Hydrogen is classified as Flammable gas Category 1 with H220 'Extremely flammable gas' and as Gases under pressure (Compressed gas) with H280 'Contains gas under pressure; may explode if heated'. Hydrogen is associated with asphyxiation in high concentrations, and the safety data sheet provides special firefighting advice and accidental release measures.

On-Site Hydrogen Production
On-site hydrogen production is the process enabled by the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0, using the electrolyser to generate hydrogen at the point of use.<SEP>On-site hydrogen production is the application of the EL 4.0, a standardised, stackable, flexible system for generating hydrogen at the point of use.

data.entity_name: AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 :: Required Hydrogen Flowrate
data.content:
AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 :: Required Hydrogen Flowrate
The required hydrogen flowrate is the hydrogen production rate that can be achieved by stacking AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 units; no numeric value or unit is stated in the source.

AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 :: Standby
Standby refers to the condition in which no hydrogen is being produced and the auxiliary components are not powered.

Auxiliary Components
Auxiliary components are parts of the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 that are not powered during standby.<SEP>Auxiliary components are parts of the EL 4.0; in the standby condition no hydrogen is produced and auxiliary components are not powered.

Modular Design
Modular design is a feature of the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 that supports stackable and flexible system setup.

Advanced Software Integration
Advanced software integration is part of the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 system and allows setup in minutes and remote control and management.

Remote Control And Management
Remote control and management is a capability of the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 enabled by advanced software integration.

Battery Limits
Battery limits is a reference that should be checked for the complete requirements list for the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.<SEP>Battery limits are referenced by footnote 2 in relation to the EL 4.0 maximum water input conductivity and the Owner's Manual.

Owners Manual
Owner’s Manual is a document that should be checked for the complete requirements list for the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.

Complete Requirements List
The complete requirements list is the full set of requirements for the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0, referenced in the Battery limits and Owner’s Manual.

S.E.P. Category
S.E.P. category is a classification to which the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 belongs according to Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU and Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.

Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU
Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU is the directive under which the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 belongs to S.E.P. category.<SEP>Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU is referenced by footnote 3 in relation to the CE mark conformity of the EL 4.0.

Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016
Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 is the regulation under which the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 belongs to S.E.P. category.<SEP>Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 is referenced by footnote 4 in relation to the UKCA mark conformity of the EL 4.0.

ETL Recognized Electrolyser Versions
ETL recognized electrolyser versions are the electrolyser versions accepted for the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.<SEP>ETL recognized electrolyser versions are the versions for which ETL recognition is applicable, as noted for CSA/ANSI B22734:2023 Ed.1 conformity.

Technical Specifications
Technical specifications describe the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0; they are under continuous improvement and might be subject to change, so the website should be consulted for the most recent specifications.

Enapter AEM Electrolyser Website
The Enapter AEM Electrolyser website, www.enapter.com/aem-electrolyser, is the source to refer to for the most recent technical specifications.

Continuous Improvement
Continuous improvement is the ongoing process affecting the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 product and its technical specifications.

ETL
ETL is the organization or mark associated with recognizing electrolyser versions for the AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.<SEP>ETL is the organization whose recognition applies to electrolyser versions for CSA/ANSI B22734:2023 Ed.1 conformity; ETL recognition is limited to recognized electrolyser versions.

Stacking
Stacking is the process of combining AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 units to achieve the required hydrogen flowrate.

AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 :: Setup Time
The AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 allows set up in minutes due to its modular design paired with advanced software integration; no specific numeric value is given.

data.entity_name: Enapter AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0 Technical Specifications (table)
data.content: Specification table for Enapter AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0. It lists hydrogen production up to 500 NL/h or 1.0785 kg/24 h, 35 barg output, 99.9% purity at 35 barg, 4.8 kWh/Nm3, 2.4 kW nominal, 3 kW peak, 0.3 kW standby, 420 mL/h water, IP20, 42 kg, and compliance/control details. It supports the surrounding claims of modular, stackable on-site hydrogen generation with remote EMS management.

EL 4.0
EL 4.0 is the Enapter AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0, a patented anion exchange membrane electrolyser, described as a standardised, stackable, flexible system for on-site hydrogen production with advanced software integration and remote control. Specifications may change because the product is under continuous improvement.

Enapter EMS
Enapter EMS is the energy management system used for fully automatic control and monitoring of the EL 4.0 via 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth and Modbus TCP over Ethernet.

Water
Water is a feedstock consumed by the EL 4.0 electrolyser, with consumption of approximately 420 mL/h at 25 °C and input pressure range of 1–4 barg.<SEP>Water is a suitable extinguishing media for hydrogen fires.<SEP>Suck back of water into the container must be prevented, and backfeed into the container must not be allowed.

Oxygen
Oxygen is an impurity monitored in the EL 4.0 hydrogen output purity specification, remaining below 5 ppm O₂ at both 35 barg and 8 barg conditions.

Water Electrolysis
Water electrolysis is the process used by the EL 4.0 to produce hydrogen, and is referenced in CSA/ANSI B22734:2023 Ed.1 for hydrogen generators using water electrolysis.

Anion Exchange Membrane
Anion exchange membrane is the patented electrolyser technology used in the EL 4.0.

Cabinet
The cabinet is part of the EL 4.0 enclosure and provides 6 U of internal space.

EL 4.0 :: Production Rate
The EL 4.0 has a production rate of up to 500 NL/h, up to 1.0785 kg/24 h, equivalent to 0.5 Nm³/h.

EL 4.0 :: Hydrogen Output Purity
The EL 4.0 hydrogen output purity is 99.9% at 35 barg with less than 1,000 ppm H₂O and less than 5 ppm O₂ at 25 °C; and 98.8% at 8 barg with less than 12,000 ppm H₂O and less than 5 ppm O₂ at 25 °C.

EL 4.0 :: Output Pressure
The EL 4.0 output pressure is up to 35 barg.

data.entity_name: EL 4.0 :: Nominal Power Consumption per Nm³ of H₂ Produced
data.content:
EL 4.0 :: Nominal Power Consumption per Nm³ of H₂ Produced
The EL 4.0 nominal power consumption per Nm³ of H₂ produced is 4.8 kWh/Nm³, beginning of life.

EL 4.0 :: Operative Power Consumption
The EL 4.0 operative power consumption is 2.4 kW, beginning of life.

EL 4.0 :: Peak Power Consumption
The EL 4.0 peak power consumption is 3 kW.

EL 4.0 :: Heat Dissipation
The EL 4.0 heat dissipation is 0.6 kW, beginning of life.

EL 4.0 :: Max Heat Dissipation
The EL 4.0 maximum heat dissipation is 0.9 kW, end of life.

EL 4.0 :: Standby Power Consumption
The EL 4.0 standby power consumption is 0.3 kW. Standby is defined as the condition in which no hydrogen is produced and auxiliary components are not powered.

EL 4.0 :: Power Supply
The EL 4.0 power supply is 220 – 240 V (AC), 50/60 Hz.

EL 4.0 :: Maximum Water Input Conductivity
The EL 4.0 maximum water input conductivity requires minimum ASTM D1193-06 Type IV water or recommended Type II or Type III water.

EL 4.0 :: Water Consumption
The EL 4.0 water consumption is approximately 420 mL/h at 25 °C.

EL 4.0 :: Water Input Pressure Range
The EL 4.0 water input pressure range is 1 – 4 barg.

EL 4.0 :: Ambient Operative Temperature Range
The EL 4.0 ambient operative temperature range is 5 °C – 45 °C.

EL 4.0 :: Ambient Operative Humidity Range
The EL 4.0 ambient operative humidity range is up to 90% humidity, non-condensing.

EL 4.0 :: IP Rating
The EL 4.0 IP rating is IP 20.

EL 4.0 :: Dimensions
The EL 4.0 dimensions are width 482 mm × depth 635 mm × height 266 mm.

EL 4.0 :: Weight
The EL 4.0 weight is 42 kg.

EL 4.0 :: Space Inside Cabinet
The EL 4.0 has 6 U of space inside the cabinet.

EL 4.0 :: Control and Monitoring
The EL 4.0 control and monitoring is fully automatic with Enapter EMS via 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth and Modbus TCP over Ethernet.

CE Mark
The CE mark is applied to the EL 4.0 according to Machine Directive 2006/42/CE; footnote 3 references Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU.

UKCA Mark
The UKCA mark is applied to the EL 4.0 according to Supply Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008; footnote 4 references Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.

CSA/ANSI B22734:2023 Ed.1
CSA/ANSI B22734:2023 Ed.1 is a standard for hydrogen generators using water electrolysis for industrial, commercial, and residential applications; conformity is limited to ETL recognized electrolyser versions.

Machine Directive 2006/42/CE
Machine Directive 2006/42/CE is the directive cited for the CE mark conformity of the EL 4.0.

Supply Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008
Supply Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 is the regulation cited for the UKCA mark conformity of the EL 4.0.

ASTM D1193-06 Type IV
ASTM D1193-06 Type IV is the minimum water quality standard required for EL 4.0 maximum water input conductivity.

ASTM D1193-06 Type II
ASTM D1193-06 Type II is a recommended water quality standard for the EL 4.0 water input.

ASTM D1193-06 Type III
ASTM D1193-06 Type III is a recommended water quality standard for the EL 4.0 water input.

Owner's Manual
The Owner's Manual is referenced by footnote 2 and contains battery limits and related information for the Enapter AEM Electrolyser EL 4.0.

2.4 GHz Wi-Fi
2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is a wireless communication interface used by the EL 4.0 for fully automatic control and monitoring via Enapter EMS.

Bluetooth
Bluetooth is a wireless communication interface used by the EL 4.0 for fully automatic control and monitoring via Enapter EMS.

Modbus TCP
Modbus TCP is a communication protocol used by the EL 4.0 for fully automatic control and monitoring via Enapter EMS over Ethernet.

Ethernet
Ethernet is the physical network medium over which the EL 4.0 provides Modbus TCP communication for control and monitoring.

Electrolyser Stack
The electrolyser stack is the stackable electrolysis assembly of the EL 4.0; performance degradation is suggested over stack lifetime by heat dissipation increasing from 0.6 kW at beginning of life to 0.9 kW maximum at end of life.

Safe Handling
Precautions for safe handling require that only experienced and properly instructed persons handle gases under pressure using properly specified equipment suitable for the product, its supply pressure and temperature.

Safe Storage
Conditions for safe storage require containers to be stored free from fire risk and away from heat and ignition sources, segregated from oxidants, protected from corrosion, and periodically checked for condition and leakage.

Purging
The system is purged with dry inert gas before gas is introduced and when placed out of service, and air is purged from the system before introducing gas.

Leak Checking
The complete system must be checked, or regularly checked, for leaks before use, and systems under pressure should be regularly checked for leakages.

Work Permit System
A work permit system, for example for maintenance activities, should be considered as an appropriate engineering control.

Ventilation
Adequate air ventilation and adequate general and local exhaust ventilation must be ensured, and containers must be kept in a well ventilated place.

Local/Regional/National/International Regulations
All regulations and local requirements regarding storage of containers must be observed, and storage must be in accordance with local, regional, national and international regulations.

Supplier's Handling Instructions
The supplier's handling instructions must be referred to when handling the product; labels provided by the supplier for identification of container contents must not be removed or defaced, and damaged valves must be reported immediately to the supplier.
